rows.about: Suit for recovery of ₹4,82,00,000 (principal ₹3,74,00,000 plus interest ₹1,08,00,000). Claims ten unpaid invoices from April 2023 to Jan 2024, illegal termination, and lapse of letter of credit. (Plaint ¶¶6,13, p.2-3)
rows.issues: Defendant's reply (Annexure P-7) denies liability: disputes invoices for Oct-Dec 2023 due to lack of joint meter readings (Reply ¶2), claims outage in Aug 2023 (Reply ¶3), and invokes arbitration clause 22 (Reply ¶6). Also, plaint claims ₹3,74,00,000 principal but legal notice (P-6) claimed ₹3,68,40,000 – discrepancy not explained. (Plaint ¶6 vs Notice ¶3). Annexures P-2 to P-5 and P-8 are not provided in this bundle.

rows.about: Key clauses: billing based on joint meter reading (cl.9.1), 30-day payment term (cl.9.2), dispute notice within 15 days (cl.9.4), late payment surcharge 1% per month (cl.9.6), letter of credit of ₹6 crore (cl.14), force majeure does not excuse payment for energy supplied (cl.18.5), arbitration clause (cl.22).
rows.issues: Defendant relies on change in law and force majeure to justify termination (Reply ¶4-5). PPA cl.18.5 says force majeure does not excuse payment for energy already supplied. Also, cl.9.3 provides that if JMR not signed within 7 days, SLDC reading is final – defendant's argument about lack of JMR may be countered. (PPA cl.9.3, cl.18.5)

rows.about: Demands payment of ₹3,68,40,000 as outstanding principal for invoices April 2023 to Dec 2023 and part-month Jan 2024, plus late payment surcharge at 1% per month. Also notes lapse of letter of credit and disputes termination. (Notice ¶¶3-5)
rows.issues: Amount claimed (₹3,68,40,000) differs from plaint's principal of ₹3,74,00,000. Notice mentions invoices up to 09.01.2024, plaint says ten invoices aggregating ₹3,74,00,000. Discrepancy may be used by defendant. (Notice ¶3 vs Plaint ¶6)

rows.about: Denies liability. Disputes invoices for Oct-Dec 2023 because meter readings were not jointly signed (Reply ¶2). Claims plant outage in Aug 2023 (Reply ¶3). Invokes arbitration clause 22 and calls for discussions (Reply ¶6). Also cites change in law and force majeure for termination (Reply ¶4-5).
rows.issues: Defendant's key arguments: (a) invoices not payable due to lack of joint meter readings (Reply ¶2); (b) outage period billed incorrectly (Reply ¶3); (c) termination valid due to change in law/force majeure (Reply ¶4-5); (d) disputes must go to arbitration, suit not maintainable (Reply ¶6). These will be used against us.

input.label: Our pleadings bundle
input.rationale: This is a court file, so the AI added a column for the annexure number, one for how much each paper matters to our case, and one for problems to watch. A plain list of file names would not help you prepare for a hearing.

columns.label: Sr.
columns.description: Running serial number of the document in the bundle.

columns.label: Document
columns.description: The name the document goes by in the case.

columns.label: Type
columns.description: What kind of paper this is: pleading, contract, notice, evidence and so on.

columns.label: Date
columns.description: The date on the document (for a series, the first date).

columns.label: Between
columns.description: Who made the document and who it is addressed to.

columns.label: Pages
columns.description: Number of pages, so you know how much there is to read.

columns.label: What it is about
columns.description: A two-line summary in plain words.

columns.label: Key terms and amounts
columns.description: The figures, clauses and phrases that matter most in this document.

columns.label: Relevance to our case
columns.description: How much this document helps (or hurts) the recovery claim.

columns.label: Annexure ref
columns.description: The annexure number it carries in the plaint.

columns.label: Issues to watch
columns.description: Gaps, mismatches or weak points the other side may use.

rows.about: The suit itself. Helios asks the court for ₹4.82 crore of unpaid invoices, interest and damages under the Power Purchase Agreement.
rows.issues: Para 31 claims 18% interest, but PPA cl. 19.2 allows only 12% on late payment. Expect the defendant to point this out.

rows.about: The signed paper that lets our lawyers appear and act for Helios in the suit.
The board agrees to sue Northgrid and names the Managing Director as the person who signs and verifies the plaint.
The contract under which Helios sells all power from its 12 MW Rajasthan solar plant to Northgrid for 25 years at a fixed tariff.
rows.issues: Cl. 22 sends disputes to arbitration. The defendant will use it to say the court should not hear the suit.

rows.about: The technical and money schedules: plant details, tariff, how each monthly bill is worked out, and the payment calendar.
rows.issues: Schedule IV in our copy is not initialled on every page. Get the signed original from the client.

rows.about: Five monthly bills for power supplied from April to August 2023. None of them has been paid.
Five more monthly bills, the last one part-month up to the termination notice. Also unpaid.
rows.issues: Invoice 10 is for 8 days of January only. Make sure the plaint total of ₹4.82 crore already reflects that.

rows.about: Helios’s own account of what Northgrid owes. It shows the last payment on 28 Mar 2023 and nothing after that.
rows.issues: A ledger kept by the plaintiff proves little on its own. It needs the Sec. 63 certificate to be admitted.

rows.about: Northgrid ends the PPA, saying a “change in law” and “deemed force majeure” (an event beyond its control) excuse it from paying.
rows.issues: The notice gives only 7 days to fix the default. PPA cl. 16.3 requires 60 days, so the termination looks invalid.

rows.about: Helios rejects the termination, demands the full ₹4.82 crore within 15 days and warns of a suit if it is not paid.
Northgrid says the invoices are “not reconciled”, repeats its termination reasons and invokes the arbitration clause.
rows.issues: First time Northgrid calls the invoices disputed. PPA cl. 9.4 gave it 15 days from each invoice to object, and it never did.

rows.about: Thirty-eight emails from Apr to Dec 2023. Northgrid acknowledges the invoices and promises payment several times.
rows.issues: Printouts of emails are admissible only with the Sec. 63 certificate (row 15). Headers are missing on 6 emails.

rows.about: Photos of the Rajasthan plant running and exporting power in December 2023, long after the date Northgrid calls force majeure.
rows.issues: No date stamp on the prints. An affidavit from whoever took them will be needed.

rows.about: Monthly readings of power sent to the grid. They back up the units charged on every invoice.
The certificate that lets the court accept the emails and ledger, which are stored on computers, as evidence.
rows.issues: The new form also needs an expert’s signature (Part B). Our copy carries only the first signature.

rows.about: An independent accountant checks the invoices against the books and certifies ₹4.82 crore as outstanding.
Receipt for the court fee paid on filing. The fee is charged as a percentage of the amount claimed.
rows.issues: Check the fee covers the pre-suit interest claimed in para 33, or the registry may ask for a top-up.

rows.about: The court issues summons to Northgrid and tells it to file a written statement (its reply to the plaint).
rows.issues: Track the date of service. The 30-day clock for the written statement runs from there.

input.label: Due-diligence data room
input.rationale: A buyer is checking the whole business, so the AI dropped the case columns. It added a risk colour, what is missing, when each paper runs out, and where it sits in the data room.

columns.label: Sr.
columns.description: Running serial number in the data room.

columns.label: Document
columns.description: The document, named as a buyer would look for it.

columns.label: Folder
columns.description: The data room folder the document is filed in.

columns.label: Counterparty
columns.description: The other side of the document: who Helios signed with or answers to.

columns.label: Risk flag
columns.description: Red needs fixing before a sale. Amber needs a look. Green is fine.

columns.label: Missing?
columns.description: Whether pages, signatures or attachments are absent.

columns.label: Valid until
columns.description: The date the document, licence or policy runs out.

columns.label: Value
columns.description: The money figure that goes with it (sum insured, loan, contract value).

columns.label: Pages
columns.description: Number of pages.

columns.label: Location
columns.description: Where to find it in the data room.

columns.label: What to check
columns.description: The one thing a buyer’s lawyer should look at first.

rows.check: The only buyer of the power has stopped paying since Mar 2023 and sent a termination notice. Suit CS(COMM) 412/2025 is pending.
Schedule IV (billing formula) is not initialled on every page. Ask for the signed original.

rows.doc: EPC contract for the solar plant
rows.check: Defects liability period ended on 31 Mar 2024. Confirm no open warranty claims and that the bank guarantee was returned.
Check whether the contractor can end the agreement if Helios’s own cash flow stays tight. Annual fee shown as value.
Only a photocopy is on file. The registered copy and the sub-registrar’s receipt are needed to prove the lease is valid.
Confirms the farm land was converted for solar use. Check the survey numbers match the lease deed.
Approved for 12 MW at the local substation. Matches the capacity in the PPA.
The renewal certificate is not in the room. Ask whether it was applied for before expiry.
Valid. Needed to claim renewable energy certificates.

rows.doc: Term loan sanction and security documents
rows.check: The loan is secured on the plant and the PPA receivables. A sale needs the lender’s consent. Check that the charge is registered with the company registry.

rows.doc: CA certificate on money owed by Northgrid
rows.check: Certifies ₹4.82 crore as unpaid up to 31 Jan 2024. The buyer should decide how to value this receivable.

rows.doc: All-risk insurance policy for the plant
rows.check: Cover for loss of profit is limited to 90 days. Check this against how long a major repair could take.
Helios is the plaintiff. Northgrid may raise the arbitration clause or file a counterclaim. Ask for the written statement when it arrives.

rows.doc: Termination notice, legal notice and reply
rows.check: Northgrid says the PPA is over. If that holds, the plant has no buyer for its power. Helios says the notice is invalid.
Minutes for FY 2022-23 are missing. They may cover the decision to keep supplying power after payments stopped.

rows.party: Income Tax Dept. and GST authorities
rows.check: Filed on time. GST was paid on the unpaid invoices; a refund route may be available if they turn into bad debt.
Not in the data room. Needed to see who must approve a sale of the company or the plant.
